name: Arma Magica
description: 'Magical defenses' based on Bonisagus's Parma Magica ritual, in which the Parma is folded upon itself to produce effects called folds; each fold is a Major Breakthrough.

name: Parma Magica
description: The Hermetic ritual of magic resistance, performed at sunrise and sunset; the only universal magic resistance known in 1220 and a key reason for the Order's success.

name: Parma Ablativa
description: The 'ablative shield' Parma fold that doubles Parma Magica for resistance but loses resistance equal to the Penetration of each resisted spell; takes ten minutes to perform.

name: Parma Absorbea
description: The 'swallowing shield' Parma fold that traps resisted spells for a round so their Penetration can empower the magus's next spell; halves Parma Magica.

name: Parma Condensa
description: The 'thick shield' Parma fold that doubles Parma Magica against one chosen Form but halves it against all others.

name: Parma Custodia
description: The 'guarding shield' Parma fold that protects against physical attacks, adding twice Parma Magica to Defense but giving no magic protection.

name: Parma Repercussa
description: The 'reflecting shield' Parma fold that bounces stopped spells back at a target the magus can see; halves Parma Magica.

name: Parma Restricta
description: The 'holding shield' Parma fold that encloses a touched target in a magical cage its spells must penetrate; often used to suppress a creature's magic.

name: Bonisagus
description: Founder of House Bonisagus who created the Parma Magica and the universal magic theory; he taught Hermetic magic to the other Founders.

name: House Bonisagus
description: The Hermetic House of researchers whose members swear to share discoveries with the Order and have the right to claim others' apprentices.

name: Parmula
description: A 'little shield': a lesser enchanted device such as a brooch granting its wearer Magic Resistance 30 for one year; a Minor Breakthrough based on Notatus's work.

name: Notatus
description: The first Primus of House Bonisagus, whose Rego Vim work and Major Breakthrough, The Aegis of the Hearth, underlie Parmulae.

name: Aegis of the Hearth
description: Ritual protecting a covenant, a Major Breakthrough of Notatus; Magvillus's Aegis is thought to be of the tenth magnitude and is suppressed on Good Friday morning.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The society of Hermetic magi, governed by the Code of Hermes, Tribunals, Primi and the Quaesitores.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The setting of the game, whose magical landscape the Order monopolizes thanks to Parma Magica.

name: Figurine Magic
description: An ancient non-Hermetic tradition, integrated via a Major Breakthrough as a Supernatural Ability, of enchanting wax or wood figurines for a specific recipient with Minor Virtues or Hermetic spells.

name: Artes Liberales
description: Ability covering the seven liberal arts, including astrology, used to prepare astrological charts for figurines.

name: Craft: Sculptor
description: Craft Ability rolled with Dexterity to carve figurines for Figurine Magic.

name: Teach
description: Ability determining how many students a teacher may teach a Parma fold at once.

name: Concentration
description: Ability used in a Stamina roll to harness spell energy trapped by the Parma Absorbea.

name: Premonitions
description: Supernatural Ability that a figurine may grant its bearer at a score of 1.

name: Second Sight
description: Supernatural Ability that a figurine may grant its bearer at a score of 1.

name: Educated
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Faerie Blood
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Gossip
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Improved Characteristic
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Large
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Latent Magic Ability
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Privileged Upbringing
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Protection
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Relic
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Skinchanger
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Social Contacts
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Student of (Realm)
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Troupe Upbringing
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: True Love
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Warrior
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Well-Traveled
description: A General Virtue from the core ArM5 rules listed as inappropriate for imbuing into a figurine via Figurine Magic.

name: Realm-Aligned Spells
description: Spells invented, as a Minor Breakthrough, to be 'flavored' to the Magic, Faerie or Infernal realm so they are unaffected by and botch less in that realm's aura.

name: Magic Realm
description: The Realm of Magic; its auras enhance Hermetic spells and realm-aligned spells can be flavored to it.

name: Divine Realm
description: The Realm whose auras suppress Hermetic spells; Hermetic magic cannot remove its influence.

name: Infernal Realm
description: The Realm of devils, whose auras suppress Hermetic spells; considered the greatest threat to the Order.

name: Faerie Realm
description: The Realm whose auras slightly enhance Hermetic spells but increase botch chances.

name: Realm Lore
description: Lore Ability for a specific realm that caps Magic Theory when inventing realm-aligned spells and reduces botch dice.

name: Faerie Lore
description: Realm Lore for the Faerie realm, used by Glaucon the Seeker to invent a faerie-aligned spell.

name: Magic Theory
description: The Ability underlying Hermetic lab work; limited by Realm Lore when inventing realm-aligned spells.

name: Glaucon the Seeker
description: Example magus who invents a faerie realm-aligned version of Sight of the Transparent Motive.

name: Sight of the Transparent Motive
description: Spell used as an example of a spell given a faerie realm-aligned version.

name: Aura
description: The supernatural influence of a Realm on a place, which modifies spellcasting and botches.

name: Regio
description: A supernatural region in which realm-aligned spells gain botch reductions like in an aura.

name: Major Breakthrough
description: A research achievement creating a new way of using Hermetic effects, such as each Parma fold or Figurine Magic.

name: Minor Breakthrough
description: A lesser research achievement not breaking the Limits of Magic, such as Parmulae or realm-aligned spells.

name: Lesser Enchanted Device
description: An enchanted item made in a single season, such as a Parmula; figurines are an alternative requiring no vis.

name: Lab Text
description: Written record of lab work; Bonisagus magi must make theirs available to all who request them.

name: Vis
description: Raw magical power used in enchantment; protected as magical property under the Code.

name: Rego
description: Hermetic Technique of control, used with Vim to create Parmulae.

name: Vim
description: Hermetic Form of magic itself, used with Rego to create Parmulae.

name: Terram
description: Hermetic Form of earth; Guernicus's earth magic was incorporated into it.

name: Mentem
description: Hermetic Form of mind; Simprim proposed Quaesitors be allowed to interrogate suspects using it.

name: Intellego
description: Hermetic Technique of perception; not the only magic that counts as scrying under the Code.

name: House Guernicus
description: The Hermetic House of judges and investigators whose members mostly hold the office of Quaesitor; motto Lex super voluntate, domus magna Magvillus.

name: Guernicus
description: Founder of House Guernicus, the last Terrae-magus, who established the Quaesitores and shaped the Code; he retired to Magvillus after the 817 AD certamen ruling.

name: Quaesitores
description: The official judges and investigators of the Order who oversee Tribunals and uphold the Code; mostly Guernicus magi plus some from other Houses.

name: Code of Hermes
description: The law of the Order: the Hermetic Oath plus the Peripheral Code of Tribunal rulings, framed by Guernicus from Germanic and Nordic tribal law; also an Ability.

name: Magvillus
description: Domus magna of House Guernicus in the Rome Tribunal, a granite fortress on an Apennine peak north of Potenza with three wards and a powerful Aegis.

name: Rome Tribunal
description: Regional Tribunal containing Magvillus; site of case rulings on Gravis, Dominicus and Helvennia.

name: Bilera
description: Archmaga and current Prima of House Guernicus, a gardener-investigator appointed to heal the Traditionalist/Transitionalist rift.

name: Traditionalists
description: Quaesitores who hold the Hermetic Oath and First Tribunal rulings as inviolable foundations of the Order.

name: Transitionalists
description: Quaesitores following Simprim who want the Code revised and Quaesitorial powers extended.

name: Fenicil
description: Favored filius of Guernicus and Primus from 832 AD, who researched ancient magical traditions and declared the Order a manifestation of an eternal organization.

name: Simprim
description: Well-respected Quaesitor who in 1148 began advocating revision of the Code, founding the Transitionalist movement.

name: Fenicil's Rituals
description: The secret rituals of House Guernicus, translated from ancient Mercurian, Egyptian, Greek and Babylonian texts; one involved human sacrifice during the Schism War.

name: Cult of Mercury
description: Ancient cult of wizards whose disbanding left the Mercurians destitute; its original thirty-eight spells are rumored in lost grimoires.

name: Mercurians
description: Remnant wizards of the Cult of Mercury who preyed on each other for spells before the Order's founding.

name: Terrae-magi
description: A small earth-wizard lineage descended from a Mercurian priest, knowing spells of earth and metal conjuring; Guernicus was its last member.

name: Gentle Gift
description: Virtue possessed by Guernicus, lacking the usual social penalty of the Gift.

name: The Gift
description: The innate capacity for magic; Guernicus thought immorality intrinsic to the Gifted nature.

name: The Thief's Tomb
description: The secret underground chamber where Guernicus entombed his master's murderer with Mercurian grimoires, guarded by an angry ghost.

name: Trianoma
description: Founder who recruited wizards to the Order with promises of Parma Magica and negotiated the creation of House Ex Miscellanea.

name: Hermetic Oath
description: The oath sworn by all magi of the Order, whose provisions form the core of the Code of Hermes.

name: Diedne
description: Founder of House Diedne and Guernicus's staunchest ally in protecting sanctum privacy.

name: House Diedne
description: Celtic Hermetic House, once the most powerful in the Order, renounced and destroyed in the Schism War.

name: Criamon
description: Founder who, with Guernicus and Diedne, demanded protection for the privacy of sanctums.

name: Peripheral Code
description: The body of Tribunal rulings that clarify, expand and embellish the Hermetic Oath.

name: Polybius
description: Greek historian (202-122 BC) whose analysis of mixed Roman government inspired Guernicus's three arms of the Order.

name: Achaean League
description: Greek league in which Polybius served as an officer.

name: Arcadia
description: District of Greece, homeland of Polybius.

name: Peloponnesus
description: Greek region the Achaean League sought to keep independent of Rome.

name: Carthage
description: City whose destruction in 146 BC Polybius witnessed.

name: Corinth
description: City whose destruction in 146 BC Polybius witnessed.

name: First Tribunal
description: The original single Tribunal of the Order (767 and 773 AD), whose rulings Traditionalists hold as foundational.

name: Grand Tribunal
description: Order-wide Tribunal formed in 773 AD, meeting at Durenmar, whose rulings bind all regional Tribunals.

name: Join or Die
description: First Tribunal ruling that magi should offer membership to peaceful wizards rather than kill them, rarely enforced.

name: Flambeau
description: Founder of House Flambeau who used Hermetic magic to purge disliked traditions and proposed Wizard War for vengeance.

name: Tytalus
description: Founder who joined Flambeau in purging non-Hermetic traditions.

name: Hariste
description: Tytalus Prima who, with Guernicus, prevented war on Pralix's Order of Miscellany.

name: Pralix
description: Leader of the 'Order of Miscellany' that became House Ex Miscellanea.

name: Order of Miscellany
description: Pralix's group of wizards, spared from war and admitted as House Ex Miscellanea.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: Hermetic House created by Trianoma's negotiation, accepting diverse non-Latin and non-Hermetic wizards and default home for vagrant magi.

name: Certamen
description: Dueling magic presented by Tremere and Bonisagus to settle disputes; declared decisive in 817 AD, later limited so it cannot override the Code.

name: Longevity Ritual
description: Ritual to extend a magus's life; Guernicus refused another after his failed.

name: Final Twilight
description: The permanent passing of a magus into Twilight, as happened to Primus Arliandus.

name: Tremere
description: Founder of House Tremere, who bid for domination of the Order and held his filii's sigils as proxy.

name: House Tremere
description: Hermetic House whose members proxy their sigils to superiors and whose conflict with House Diedne led to the Schism War.

name: The Sundering
description: Event of 848 AD ending Tremere's bid for domination of the Order.

name: Cult of Thoth
description: Ancient Egyptian cult Fenicil identified as a forerunner of the Order.

name: Hermes Trismegistus
description: Figure whose writings Fenicil researched to find the Order's ancient foundations.

name: Bjornaer
description: One of the two non-Latin Founders.

name: House Bjornaer
description: Non-Latin Hermetic House potentially threatened by a Latin-only movement.

name: Schism War
description: The war between the Order and House Diedne, triggered by conflict with House Tremere, in which House Diedne fell.

name: Duresca
description: Covenant in Iberia where the Duresca Scrolls were discovered in the 10th century.

name: Duresca Scrolls
description: Letters purportedly between Guernicus and his filii revealing a plan to dominate the Order, declared fraudulent by the Iberian Tribunal.

name: Iberian Tribunal
description: Regional Tribunal that declared the Duresca Scrolls fraudulent.

name: Iberia
description: Region where Duresca lies and where Bilera uncovered diabolists.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House whose purging in the 10th century distracted the Order.

name: Antonius
description: Guernicus Primus during the Schism War who called the emergency Grand Tribunal and led Fenicil's sacrificial ritual.

name: Hoplites
description: Warrior magi who guard Magvillus and aid Guernicus advocates.

name: House Mercere
description: The Hermetic House of Redcaps who carry messages and notices between magi.

name: Redcaps
description: Members of House Mercere, often without magic resistance, who deliver messages and declarations and act as proxies and witnesses.

name: Presiding Quaesitor
description: The Quaesitor presiding over a Tribunal who is the authority on the Code and wields a veto.

name: Primus
description: Head of a Hermetic House; Primi are one of the three arms of the Order.

name: Arliandus
description: Previous Primus of House Guernicus and leader of the Traditionalists, who passed into Final Twilight.

name: Jart
description: Filius of Arliandus who now leads the Traditionalist faction.

name: Apennine Mountains
description: Mountain range in whose southern portion Magvillus lies.

name: Kingdom of Sicily
description: Kingdom containing Magvillus.

name: Potenza
description: Town about nine miles south of Magvillus.

name: Charlemagne
description: Ruler from whose time no noble has dared attack Magvillus.

name: Automata
description: Hermetic enchanted constructs provided by Verditius Quaesitors to defend Magvillus.

name: Earth Elementals
description: Powerful spirits thought to inhabit Magvillus's mountain, allies of Guernicus and loyal to his heirs.

name: Verditius
description: Founder who insisted on the Code's prohibition of scrying to protect his tradition's secrets.

name: Nicholas of Myra
description: Saint to whom Magvillus's chapel is dedicated, whose altar holds a shard of the brine barrel from his miracle.

name: Magvillus Council
description: Two-tier council ruling House Guernicus: an inner tier of six Guernicus magi plus the Primus, and an outer tier of twenty-four.

name: Casting Tokens
description: Invested transport devices given to outer council members that serve as tokens for Magvillus's Aegis of the Hearth.

name: The Imperfect Defense
description: Secret that a Divine aura suppresses Magvillus's Aegis for two hours before sunrise on Good Friday.

name: Jesus
description: Whose trial by the Sanhedrin may correspond to the Good Friday Divine aura at Magvillus.

name: Rome
description: City to which Guernicus reputedly made pilgrimage and where Bilera uncovered diabolists.

name: Transylvania
description: Region where Bilera uncovered diabolists.

name: Diabolists
description: Infernalists who are often declared enemies of the Order.

name: Archmagus
description: Title of a highly accomplished magus, held by Bilera.

name: Forfeit Immunity
description: Loss of legal protection under Hermetic Law, e.g. during Wizard War, when committing a crime, or when intruding in a sanctum.

name: Wizard War
description: A declared month-long open conflict in which two magi may legally slay each other.

name: Wizard's March
description: The penalty of casting out a magus to be hunted, possible only for high crimes.

name: High Crimes
description: Clear and direct breaches of the Code, such as slaying a magus or dealing with devils, which permit a Wizard's March.

name: Low Crimes
description: All offenses other than high crimes, which cannot result in a Wizard's March.

name: Sanctum
description: A magus's private laboratory space whose privacy is protected; intruders forfeit immunity.

name: Gravis of House Flambeau
description: Magus who slew the prankster Talus with a Ball of Abyssal Flame and was later slain by Dominicus.

name: Talus of House Merinita
description: Prankster magus slain by Gravis after changing his voice with a spell.

name: Dominicus of House Jerbiton
description: Magus who slew Gravis in 891 AD and was acquitted of seeking retribution by Wizard War in 898 AD.

name: House Flambeau
description: Hermetic House of Gravis.

name: House Merinita
description: Hermetic House of Talus and Guardinia.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House of Dominicus.

name: Ball of Abyssal Flame
description: Fire spell used by Gravis to slay Talus and to attack Dominicus.

name: Clenching Hand of the Crushed Heart
description: Spell Dominicus used to slay Gravis instantly.

name: Amicus
description: A magus sworn in an oath of friendship to another, implying a lasting moral duty of support and vengeance.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Regional Tribunal known for the Rhine Corruption of proxy votes and the Hernis and Rudophus cases.

name: Hernis
description: Rhine magus convicted of endangering the Order through excessive Wizard War and hunted down.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: Regional Tribunal where Dominicus and Berenguer were tried.

name: Proxy Voting
description: Giving one's sigil to another magus to vote on one's behalf, as a directed or free proxy.

name: Sigil
description: A magus's token of voting rights at Tribunal, which can be given as a proxy.

name: Durenmar
description: Covenant where the Grand Tribunal meets and whose library receives Bonisagus texts.

name: Stonehenge Tribunal
description: Tribunal on the England-Scotland border region.

name: Loch Leglean Tribunal
description: Tribunal on the England-Scotland border region.

name: England
description: Kingdom bordering Scotland, used as an example of vague Tribunal borders.

name: Scotland
description: Kingdom bordering England, used as an example of vague Tribunal borders.

name: Praeco
description: The magus who chairs a Tribunal meeting, summarizes cases, breaks tied votes and can exclude misbehaving magi.

name: Vagrancy
description: The low crime of lacking a House or residential Tribunal, which can lead to a March if uncorrected.

name: True Lineages
description: Houses such as Bonisagus, Guernicus, Mercere and Tremere whose members never sponsor magi to join them.

name: The Rhine Corruption
description: Practice in the Rhine Tribunal of keeping the proxy votes of dead magi ('sigil ghosts') to accumulate votes.

name: Rudophus of Durenmar
description: Magus convicted of endangering the Order after a demon he pursued attacked the Rhine Redcaps.

name: Demons
description: Infernal agents with whom magi are absolutely forbidden to deal.

name: Faeries
description: The fay, whom magi are forbidden to molest lest their vengeance fall on other magi.

name: Guardinia of Merinita
description: Maga who accused Berenguer of Tytalus of molesting the fay.

name: Berenguer of Tytalus
description: Magus acquitted of molesting the fay after rescuing his apprentice from faeries.

name: Invisible Eye Revealed
description: Spell to reveal scrying, considered a legal protection within a covenant.

name: Sight of True Form
description: Spell considered a reasonable covenant defense against magical spying.

name: Forceless Casting
description: Casting without Penetration to avoid affecting protected magi when scrying.

name: Gauntlet
description: The test an apprentice passes to become a magus.

name: Blood Rights
description: Example case of a maga's claim to her own Gifted child against a magus's formal claim of apprenticeship.

name: Helvennia of Bonisagus
description: Maga who claimed eight apprentices, all of whom died; acquitted but slain after seven Wizard Wars were declared on her.

name: Case Rulings
description: Tribunal rulings arising from convictions or acquittals in criminal cases.

name: Proposal Rulings
description: Tribunal rulings proposed for debate, which must be published two years in advance.

name: Guernicus Advocate
description: A Guernicus magus who defends absent defendants or clients with strong cases.

name: Testimony of Testimony
description: Written testimony read out by a principle at Tribunal on behalf of an absent witness.

name: Hermes Lore
description: Ability in which Quaesitor candidates are trained.

name: Awareness
description: Ability in which Quaesitor candidates are trained.

name: Folk Ken
description: Ability in which Quaesitor candidates are trained.

name: Intrigue
description: Ability in which Quaesitor candidates are trained.

name: Roman Empire
description: Failing empire in which the impoverished Terrae-magi lived.

name: Familiar
description: A magus's magical companion, protected as magical property; Gravis was punished by its death.
